To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p05
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — please do not enter 43

Mick, please don’t go into 43 at 9, with or without the props, and please don’t take your lad in. Priya, please don’t arrange access for this. No loft inspection from inside either.

I’m chartered with IStructE, but I’m speaking as a neighbour who looked from the opposite pavement at about 7, not as an appointed engineer. This isn’t a commission; I have no PI cover for informal advice, and this is not a structural assessment or an assurance of safety.

Part of 41’s chimney is still standing, leaning towards 43, with visibly poor mortar at its base. It could fall further. There’s a substantial hole in 43’s roof, a stepped crack above the bay and apparent movement at the bay head. These are observations, not measurements from an inspection.

Standing under that damaged roof and loose stack to put props in is about the worst place to be. Floors may already be carrying fallen masonry, and we don’t know how loads are now being carried through the building. Props placed without assessment could make matters worse. Victorian terraces can be robust, as Jo’s cousin says, but this is a damaged terrace.

Priya: I cannot say 45 is safe. Its front looks undamaged, but I couldn’t see the shared wall. Mrs Doherty’s decision isn’t mine, but I would not sleep in her front room tonight; staying with family until 45 has been checked would be better.

Loose slates remain above the footway at 43 and 45. The garden tape does not make the pavement safe. Please use the opposite side, especially on the school run.

The council already knows, but nobody has closed the footway. Please urgently update dangerous structures via the main council number and ask for protection of the pavement. If anything starts falling or there’s immediate danger, call 999 and keep clear.
---
To: dm:Gary_41
Replying to: d01
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — urgent safety information

Gary, I won’t put your private message on the forum. But please tell the council’s dangerous structures officer about the chimney breast removals and brackets immediately, before anyone enters. That information matters to their assessment. It doesn’t establish why the collapse happened, and I can’t advise on insurance. Please don’t go inside to investigate or collect paperwork. A private conversation mustn’t delay getting that information to them.
